dos: Do spend Signal Red only on times, status, and one action per viewport.
Do set every comparable numeral tabular (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums).
Do theme browser surfaces from the palette: red text selection, red focus rings, ink scrollbar, 4px underline offsets.
Do quote code and commands verbatim from the package READMEs; abridge openly, never paraphrase APIs.
Do keep the primary action inside the departure band, above the fold.
donts: Don't build centered headline-plus-card heroes or equal icon-plus-text card rows; the timetable is the composition.
Don't put kickers or eyebrows above headings; headings carry their own weight.
Don't use gradient text, glass blur, or hard offset block shadows anywhere in this world.
Don't invent testimonials, benchmarks, pricing, or availability claims the READMEs do not make.
Don't let code wells scroll the page; overflow scrolls inside the well.
keyCharacteristics: Timetable grammar: platforms, lines, termini, connections, exact versions as times.
One dark band, one red, paper everywhere else.
Tabular numerals on all data; mono for code, times, and spec labels.
Precision over warmth; copy stays technical and minimal.
narrative.overview: Every surface reads as an exact railway timetable, not a marketing hero. Packages are lines with termini, connections, and honest times; precision is the persuasion. The page opens on a dark ink departure band and continues on near-white paper ruled with hairlines, so density lives in the board and air lives everywhere else. Type is a grotesk-first system voice with tabular numerals wherever data appears; the single signal red is spent only on times and status, never on decoration. Motion is one authored moment: selecting a departure sweeps the highlight across board row, spec strip, and map stops together. Everything else is instant and legible by default.

rules.body: Signal red appears on times, status, and one action per viewport. Anything else wanting emphasis uses weight or size.
rules.name: The One Red Rule

rules.body: Any numeral a visitor compares (versions, times, specs) sets tabular-nums. Proportional figures never appear in data.
rules.name: The Tabular Data Rule

rules.body: A surface is either the board (lift) or a card (rest) or flat paper. No intermediate shadows exist.
rules.name: The Two Altitudes Rule
